w03.129: **The Deity of the Supreme Being.** Having completed His evolution, this Deity carries within Himself the whole of finite experience and all the experiential power that was earned, because these evolutionary qualities have become one with the spirit person bestowed by the Paradise Trinity on the finite level as God the Supreme.
w03.130: In this way the first experiential Trinity holds the entire original endowment of Paradise divinity, enriched by passage through the “Supreme Adventure.” Here, then, is the second thesis: a challenge that, at the dawn of the third age, advances to the frontier of a new creation and opens the “Ultimate Adventure.”
w03.131: 4. The Nature of the Ultimate Trinity (orig. pp. 70–71)
w03.133: The Ultimate Trinity is something truly new in the universe, because it is an experiential Trinity; the original Paradise Trinity is existential. The Urantia Book calls it both the Ultimate Trinity and the Trinity Ultimate, and the Foreword describes it as not yet fully disclosed, still in the course of being realized.
w03.135: The two Trinities compared (as Sadler arranges them)
w03.140: Formed at the end of the second age; unity won by effort in the outer space ages
w03.142: The Ultimate Trinity can take form as a factual reality when the second age ends, but its unified status must be won through experiential effort and achievement across the post-Supreme ages on all four outer space levels. It aims at bringing the whole master universe to full development. To succeed in that is the development of the Trinity itself, the completion of its unity, and from it there emerges God the Ultimate, the second experiential Deity. Just as the Supreme appears once the grand universe reaches maturity, the Ultimate appears once the master universe does.
w03.144: Sadler states that the Ultimate, like the Supreme, has long been present in Havona. The text says that Havona is a finished portrayal of the Supreme’s future perfection and “⟦Q 14:6.25⟧is suggestive of the potential of the Ultimate⟦/Q⟧” [14:6.25]. Sadler’s statement is an interpretation that carries this hint one step further.
w03.146: For the first time in universe history, the Paradise Trinity and the Ultimate Trinity will work together for the master universe on the absonite level. The Paradise Trinity has functioned existentially on that level from eternity. Sadler expects that the Paradise Trinity will withdraw to the extent that the Ultimate Trinity becomes able to function experientially. The picture resembles parents handing tasks over to a growing child, but it is not something the text says.
w03.147: The relationship with God the Sevenfold
w03.148: The Urantia Book puts forward fairly clearly the idea that God the Sevenfold will extend His function in the post-Supreme ages by serving the creations of outer space.
w03.150: How God the Sevenfold will be related to the Ultimate Trinity, however, is a matter for speculation. Because the two Trinities will co-operate in the outer universes, Sadler thinks it likely that God the Sevenfold will maintain a co-operative relationship with each of them. Of one thing only is he confident: that new domain will see vigorous activity by the Master Spirits and the Creator Sons.
w03.151: 5. The Second Nuclear Universe: A Power Base (orig. pp. 71–72)
w03.152: Deity works outward from a base
w03.153: Sadler observes that Deity always seems to act from a power base, a foundation from which divinity and sovereignty can extend. A Trinity is Deity too, and so is no exception to this general rule. The existential Trinity works from the base of the Paradise-Havona system, and Havona becomes the nuclear universe from which that activity widens outward. The Urantia Book likewise calls Havona and Paradise the “power nucleus” of all later expansion.
w03.155: The first experiential Trinity will work from a comparable base, the grand universe in its role as second nuclear universe, holding existential-experiential status.
w03.156: How the completed synthesis differs from the new thesis
w03.157: To the Father’s invitation and command, “Be you perfect,” the superuniverses complete their first response, the finite response, by the third age. Having reached the (relative) perfection of settlement in light and life, they become, together with Havona, a nucleus unified on the finite level: the grand universe.
w03.158: How does the grand universe as completed synthesis differ from the grand universe as new thesis? Sadler asks us to recall Havona in the first age and Havona in the second. The earlier Havona was isolated and self-sufficient; the later Havona was a nucleus whose citizens reached out into the cytoplasmic superuniverses. Likewise the grand universe, as the second age closes, enjoys the contentment of a destiny achieved, and as the third age opens it is mobilized to meet the “Ultimate Adventure.” Sadler sums this up as a passage from the static state of “destiny attained” to the dynamic state of “destiny pursued.”
w03.159: New growth coming to the grand universe
w03.160: Having become a nucleus, the grand universe will undergo a new kind of growth through its relationship with the outer universes. In the first age Havona was held in the existential stalemate of flawless perfection, but during the second age the time pilgrims broke through that limit by bringing in experiential growth. Sadler expects Havona to break through a limit to its growth a second time when the first beings from outer space arrive in the central universe. The superuniverses too, whose growth comes to rest in light and life, will on their arrival enter upon a new growth that goes beyond the finite. This is speculation about an unrevealed future, but speculation modeled on what actually happened in Havona.
w03.161: 6. Features of Nucleus and Cytoplasm (orig. pp. 72–73)
w03.162: The superuniverses, which have been both
w03.163: The superuniverses show most clearly how a nuclear creation differs from a cytoplasmic universe, because they pass through both conditions. In the second age, as cytoplasm to Havona, they were the domain of the most intense creative activity. What on Paradise, or among the billion worlds of Havona, could compare with the creativity that poured forth from seven hundred thousand local universes? To say nothing of the reproductive activity that must have flourished among the midsoniters and Material Sons across seven billion local systems, and among mortal races on seven trillion inhabited worlds.
w03.164: As the superuniverses pass from cytoplasm to a share in the new nucleus, however, creativity, and perhaps reproductive activity as well, must slow down. They are moving gradually toward a more settled and stable status, one that in some measure resembles the stability of the central universe.
w03.165: This transition shows most plainly in the local universes. If, as Sadler believes, the Creator Sons and Creative Spirits depart for outer space, the local universes will become stable administrative units, like the sectors of a superuniverse. Creative activity will not cease, but it will be greatly reduced.
w03.166: Features of nuclear and cytoplasmic universes (as Sadler arranges them)
w03.168: (Relative) instability that comes with rapid growth and change
w03.171: Power base; sends out pioneering personnel
Frontier of new creation; receives pioneering personnel
w03.172: Havona in the second age; the grand universe in the third age
The superuniverses in the second age; outer space from the third age on
w03.174: The nucleus is mature; the cytoplasm is not yet. A nuclear universe is the foundation for outward expansion, and from it the leading creators, their co-ordinates, and their subordinates go forth to the frontiers of a new creation. It is like a full-grown tree that no longer grows taller yet scatters its seeds far and wide to raise a new forest.
w03.175: 7. Mobilization and the Advance into Outer Space (orig. pp. 73–74)
w03.176: Recalling the anticipation before the first adventure
w03.177: When time began, expectation must have filled the entire Paradise-Havona system on the eve of the “Supreme Adventure.” Sadler reminds us that those who descended were all personalities. From the Ancients of Days down to the supernaphim who volunteered, they possess imagination, are somewhat unpredictable in their choices, and are even capable of choosing evil. The text makes this clear even for beings above the rank of a Creator Son.
w03.179: Their work was therefore a true adventure, tested in the face of the unknown.
w03.180: The mobilization of the grand universe
w03.181: A similar experience awaits the grand universe in the distant future. As soon as the first experiential Trinity starts marshaling the powers and personalities of the second nuclear universe, the “quiet time” between universe ages will draw toward its close. Sadler admits he can only speculate, but he holds that the text supplies grounds for reasonable conjecture. Indeed, the authors of the text make no secret of their belief that the Corps of the Finality will serve in outer space.
w03.184: Sadler pictures it this way. The mobilization first becomes visible as the finaliters withdraw, very gradually, from superuniverse service and gather on Paradise. The Ultimate Trinity commands the Mortal Corps of the Finality together with all six of the other corps. Many personalities of single and dual origin leave their posts as well, and administrators of Trinity origin fill the places they vacate.
w03.185: At last all seven Corps of the Finality are assembled on Paradise. From Creator Sons to midwayers and mortal finaliters, veterans tested through two universe ages come together in one place, perhaps for the first and only time. Sadler suggests that they will then be commissioned to create, organize, and administer the universes of outer space, and that the order to proceed may be issued by the master universe’s senior Architect. Since the text states that the senior Master Architect has oversight of all seven finaliter corps [31:10.1], this is not groundless imagining.
w03.186: Once the order is given, the great departure from Paradise begins. Wave upon wave, they pass through the circuits of Havona and the superuniverses settled in light and life, cross the quiet zone that encircles the grand universe, and stream out into the vastness of the Primary Space Level.
w03.187: The sequence of mobilization and great migration as Sadler imagines it; all of it is conjecture about an unrevealed future
w03.188: Sadler and the text: on the paragraphs cited
w03.189: In this chapter Sadler cites several paragraphs in support. For the composite nature of Michael he cites 119:8.8, which names in turn a Melchizedek, a system savior, an Adamic redeemer, a seraphic fellow, a morontia progressor, and a Son of Man. The name “Lanonandek” does not appear there, but “system savior” refers to the bestowal in the likeness of a Lanonandek Son, so Sadler’s summary is consistent with it. For the mobilization he cites 31:10.1, which is a single line stating that the senior Master Architect oversees the seven Corps of the Finality. The substantive textual basis for service in outer space is better sought in 31:10.13 and 31:10.19 of the same section.
w03.190: The emergence of the Supreme Being brings four factors onto the absonite level: the first experiential Trinity, the personal activity of the Supreme Being, the Corps of Supreme Creators, and post-finite creatures.
w03.191: The Supreme Creators have become experiential beings by evolving along with their domains; a Creator Son becoming a Master Son is the typical case, as with Michael of Nebadon.
w03.192: The Ultimate Trinity consists of the Deity of the Corps of Master Architects, the Deity of the Corps of Supreme Creators, and the Deity of the Supreme Being. It involves 1,428,040 personalities, yet it is a union of Deity, not of persons.
w03.193: Being experiential, the Ultimate Trinity grows and learns; it achieves unity by bringing the whole master universe to completion, and so leads to the emergence of God the Ultimate.
w03.194: Sadler conjectures that while the two Trinities co-operate, the Paradise Trinity will gradually withdraw from function, and that God the Sevenfold will co-operate with both Trinities.
w03.195: Deity works from a power base. As the second nuclear universe, the completed grand universe passes from the static state of “destiny attained” to the dynamic state of “destiny pursued.”
w03.196: A nuclear universe is stable and mature and sends out pioneering personnel; a cytoplasmic universe is unstable but at the height of creative activity.
w03.197: Sadler pictures, as conjecture, a scene of mobilization: the finaliters withdraw and assemble on Paradise, receive their commissions and the order to proceed, and set out in a great migration to outer space.
